title: What is TV PDF Viewer for Roku?
content: TV PDF Viewer turns a Roku device with USB support into a simple digital signage player. Add photos, videos, and optional audio files to a USB drive, connect it to your Roku device, and use the app to play a clean signage loop on your TV.

title: How does TV PDF Viewer work?
content: The app scans your connected USB drive, finds supported signage media across folders and subfolders, and builds a playback loop. Images and videos are used as the visual signage loop, while audio files can be used as optional background music during image playback.

title: Do I need an internet connection to play USB signage?
content: Local USB playback does not require a separate media server or cloud dashboard. However, an internet connection may be needed for Roku subscription purchase and validation, Help / FAQ, Privacy Policy, Terms of Use, and support or feedback links.

title: Do all Roku devices support USB playback?
content: No. TV PDF Viewer needs a Roku device or Roku TV that can read media from a USB drive. Many Roku TVs and some Roku players include USB support, while smaller streaming sticks usually do not have a USB port for media playback.

title: Which USB drive format should I use?
content: For best compatibility, use a FAT32-formatted USB drive. Roku USB storage support can vary by device model and Roku OS version, so if your drive is not detected, try a dedicated FAT32 drive with your signage files copied onto it.

title: Why is my USB drive not detected?
content: Make sure your Roku device supports USB media, the drive is connected firmly, the drive is readable by Roku, and the drive has enough power. Large portable hard drives may require external power or a powered USB hub. If detection still fails, try reformatting the drive as FAT32 and reconnecting it.

title: What should I put on the USB drive?
content: Add the photos and videos you want to show on screen. You can also add audio files if you want background music while images are displayed. For predictable playback order, use clear filenames such as 001-welcome.jpg, 002-menu.mp4, and 003-offer.png.

title: Does the app scan folders and subfolders?
content: Yes. The app is designed to scan folders and subfolders so you can organize your USB drive while still creating one signage-ready media list.

title: Can I use photos and videos in the same signage loop?
content: Yes. The signage player can play a mixed visual loop of images and videos from your USB drive.

title: Can I use audio as background music?
content: Yes. Audio files on the USB drive can play as background music while image slides are being shown. Audio files are optional, so the app also works with only photos and videos.

title: What happens to background music when a video plays?
content: When a video plays, the app stops or releases background audio so the video's own sound can be heard. When the signage loop returns to image playback, background audio can continue again.

title: Can videos play with their own sound?
content: Yes. Videos play through Roku video playback and can use their own audio track. Background music is not mixed over the video.

title: How does the app decide playback order?
content: The signage list is sorted by filename. Visual media such as images and videos play in filename order. Audio files are used separately as a background music list.

title: Can I control the playback order?
content: Yes. Rename your files to control the order. Numbered prefixes work well, for example 001-intro.jpg, 002-product.mp4, 003-hours.png, and 004-promo.jpg.

title: What image file types can the app recognize?
content: The app recognizes image extensions including JPG, JPEG, JPE, JIF, JFIF, JFI, PNG, APNG, GIF, WebP, BMP, DIB, TIF, TIFF, AVIF, HEIF, and HEIC. Recognition is based on file extension, and actual display support depends on Roku's platform support for that image format.

title: What video file types can the app recognize?
content: The app recognizes video extensions including MP4, AVI, MKV, MOV, FLV, WMV, WebM, M4V, 3GP, TS, MTS, M2TS, MPG, MPEG, VOB, and OGV. Recognition is based on file extension, and actual playback depends on whether your Roku device supports the video's container, video codec, and audio codec.

title: What audio file types can the app recognize?
content: The app recognizes audio extensions including MP3, M4A, AAC, OGG, OGA, OPUS, FLAC, WAV, WebM, MKV, MKA, TS, 3GP, AMR, WMA, and ALAC. Recognition is based on file extension, and actual playback depends on Roku codec support.

title: Why does a file appear but not play?
content: The app may recognize a file extension even when Roku cannot decode the actual media inside the file. For best video compatibility, use common Roku-friendly files such as MP4 with H.264 video and AAC audio.

title: Why does a video play without sound?
content: This usually means the video track is compatible but the audio track is not supported by your Roku device or connected audio system. Try converting the video to use a broadly supported audio format such as stereo AAC.

title: Are DRM-protected files supported?
content: No. DRM-protected movies, music, or other protected media files are not supported for local USB signage playback.

title: Does the app hide system files?
content: Yes. The app skips dot-prefixed hidden files and common system folders such as lost.dir, System Volume Information, and $Recycle.Bin so they do not clutter the signage library.

title: Why do I see a No USB Connected message?
content: This means the app could not find a readable USB drive. Confirm that your Roku device supports USB storage, connect a compatible USB drive, and use Reload Files after reconnecting the drive.

title: Why do I see an empty folder or no playable media message?
content: This means the USB drive was found, but the app did not find playable signage media. Add images, videos, and optional audio files, then choose Reload Files from the menu.

title: What does Reload Files do?
content: Reload Files rescans the USB drive from the USB root. Use it after adding, removing, renaming, or reorganizing files on the USB drive.

title: Can I start playback from the menu?
content: Yes. Choose Play from the left menu to start signage playback from the current USB media list. You can also select playable USB media from the grid.

title: What happens if there are only audio files on the USB drive?
content: The signage player needs at least one image or video for the visual loop. If no playable images or videos are available, the app shows a Signage Unavailable message.

title: Can I change how long each image stays on screen?
content: Yes. Open Settings and adjust Slide Duration. The default duration is 3 seconds, and the app prevents the duration from going below 1 second.

title: Can I change how images fit the screen?
content: Yes. Open Settings and choose Fill Screen or Show Full Image. Fill Screen fills the TV and may crop the image. Show Full Image preserves the complete image and may show borders if the image aspect ratio does not match the TV.

title: Can I change the image background color?
content: Yes. Open Settings and choose a black or white background. This is most visible when Show Full Image mode leaves empty space around an image.

title: Are settings saved?
content: Yes. Slide duration, image display mode, and background color are saved on the Roku device, so your choices remain available after restarting the app.

title: Why do some items show a lock icon?
content: Locked items appear when the free access limit has been reached. Subscribe through Roku to unlock larger USB media collections.

title: What are the free access limits?
content: Free access includes limited playback from the USB media list. In the current app, recursive signage mode allows the first 5 image files, first 2 video files, and first 2 audio files before additional items are locked.

title: What does the subscription unlock?
content: A Roku subscription unlocks fuller access to larger USB collections so more of your photos, videos, and audio files can be included in the signage experience.

title: How do I subscribe?
content: Choose Subscribe from the app menu or from the lock-limit dialog. The app uses Roku's Channel Store purchase flow and shows available subscription plans from the Roku catalog.

title: What subscription plans can appear?
content: The subscription screen can show Roku catalog products such as monthly, quarterly, half-yearly, or yearly plans, depending on what is configured and available in the Roku Channel Store.

title: How do I manage or cancel my subscription?
content: Use Manage Subscription in the app for guidance. On your Roku device, you can also highlight TV PDF Viewer on the Roku Home screen, press the * button, and choose Manage subscription when available.

title: Why do I see a demo watermark?
content: A demo watermark may appear during signage playback when the app is running without an active Roku subscription. Subscribed users should not see the demo watermark.

title: Does the app upload my USB files?
content: No. USB media playback is local to your Roku device. The app does not upload your photos, videos, or audio files to a cloud dashboard.

title: Does the app include a remote web dashboard?
content: No. TV PDF Viewer is focused on simple USB-based playback. It does not include cloud sync, remote web management, or network file sharing.

title: Can I schedule different playlists by time or date?
content: No. The current app is designed for a simple continuous USB signage loop. Time-based scheduling is not part of the current feature set.

title: Can the app edit, resize, or convert media files?
content: No. The app plays media from your USB drive but does not edit, resize, repair, or convert files. If a file is too large or not compatible, convert it on a computer before copying it to the USB drive.

title: How can I make playback smoother?
content: Use compressed media files close to your TV's display resolution, avoid extremely large images or high-bitrate videos on lower-powered Roku devices, and use a dedicated USB drive for signage content.

title: Where can I get support?
content: Open Support & Feedback from the app menu. The page includes a QR code for the support page and a QR code for the feedback form.

title: Where can I send feedback or suggestions?
content: Open Support & Feedback in the app and scan the Feedback Form QR code. You can also use the feedback contact shown on the About Us page.

title: Where can I read the Privacy Policy and Terms of Use?
content: Privacy Policy and Terms of Use are available from the app menu. These pages load the latest published documents and may require an internet connection.

title: What information is shown on the About Us page?
content: The About Us page shows the TV PDF Viewer app name, app tagline, app icon, developer credit, icon and menu icon credits, and feedback contact information.
